Detachment of Device or Device Component
records.text: Philips received a report that more than half of the Quadrature Body Coil (QBC) rubber inside the magnet had peeled off. This seal is used for protection, to avoid the patient from potentially contacting the sharp edges of the Magnet covers.If this seal is peeling off, it is likely that this could lead to serious injury. The QBC rubber that was peeled off, was cleaned and secured in place and the system was handed back to the customer for use.The failure of the QBC seal to remain in place is considered a malfunction.Remedial action:A field action was initiated under 2023-PD-MR-013.A Field Safety Notification was sent to the customers informing them about this potential issue.The updated Field correction has been made available to the field in Dec 2025 in the event country (the affected market).

product_problems: Insufficient Device Problem Information
records.text: Siemens Healthineers (Siemens) was notified of a patient health event associated with an examination performed using a MAGNETOM Sola MRI system. According to the customer, the patient had a known history of allergies to latex and perfumes/fragrances.Shortly after the examination, the patient developed tingling and itching of the hands, which progressed to generalized pruritus and worsening symptoms. Subsequently, the patient experienced widespread raised skin lesions and significant respiratory difficulty. The patient sought treatment at an Urgent Care facility, where she received adrenaline, hydrocortisone (100 mg), and chlorphenamine.The patient reported that she was formally diagnosed with anaphylaxis following the event and was subsequently prescribed an EpiPen. The symptoms resolved within approximately one hour, and the patient made a full recovery. Due to the severity of the reaction and the requirement for emergency medical intervention, this event is considered reportable. H3, H6: The investigation is ongoing. A supplemental report will be submitted upon receipt of additional reportable information and/or investigation completion.

product_problems: Insufficient Device Problem Information
records.text: Siemens Healthineers (Siemens) was notified of a patient injury associated with a cerebral infarction and head examination performed using the MAGNETOM Mica MRI system on (b)(6) 2026. The patient is described as a female in her fifties. On (b)(6) 2026, swelling of the patient¿s arm was observed. A CT examination was subsequently performed, which revealed fractures of the left humerus and left tibia. On (b)(6) 2026, Siemens was informed that the patient¿s arm was fractured. In combination with the onsite assessment of the MRI by the local Customer Service Engineer and analysis by Siemens R&D experts, no abnormalities or malfunctions were identified in the MRI system, including the patient table. The patient¿s injury is classified as a severe injury, and Siemens could not determine whether this injury was caused by the MRI system or not. Siemens has requested additional event information and what medical intervention the patient received to treat the fractures. Additional information has not been received as of the date of this report. E1: A facility contact name was not provided for reporting. G3 510(k): The MAGNETOM Mica is not cleared for sale in the USA by the FDA (does not have a 510(k). This system is similar to the MAGNETOM Altea, 510(k) K252838. H6: A supplemental report will be submitted if additional reportable information is obtained either from the customer or through further investigation.

Insufficient Device Problem Information
records.text: Philips received a report that the patient suffered a burn to the outer left thigh during the examination. Unspecified treatment was provided, and the burn is expected to heal completely. A photograph provided with the report shows a small burn with three distinct contact points, exhibiting skin dimpling, blackening, and a waxy appearance. It was also reported that the patient did not have access to the nurse call light and that skin-to-coil contact occurred during the procedure. No medical intervention beyond the unspecified treatment was reported; however, based on the current clinical standard of care, the characteristics of the reported burn indicate a level of clinical severity for which referral to a specialized burn center or inpatient hospitalization may be warranted to prevent permanent impairment. Therefore, the reported event meets the criteria for a serious injury and this event has been determined to be reportable. Philips has started an investigation, a follow up report will be submitted once the investigation has been completed.

product_problems: Excessive Heating
records.text: I am filing a formal patient safety complaint about an MRI at (b)(6) on (b)(6) 2026. Approximatelyone to two weeks earlier I presented for this exam on two separate appointments andwas turned away both times because the MRI machine was not working. I wasrescheduled. On this visit I was placed in that same machine. I was not given anemergency call bulb or call button. While in the scanner I felt warmth in my left arm thatbecame progressively hotter. I have had MRI examinations before and have neverexperienced this sensation. Because this unit had already been out of service at mytwo prior visits, I reported the heating immediately so that I would be removed before aninjury occurred. Staff could not hear me. I had to call out several times. I was told thesensation was normal. Staff remained focused on completing the remainingapproximately four minutes of the exam rather than stopping the scan and taking meout of the magnet. With no call bulb and no response to my concern, I had to get myselfout of the machine. The examination was not completed. My knee is now swollen. I amobtaining medical documentation. I was offered another reschedule. I am not refusing amedically necessary MRI. I do not accept a reschedule as resolution of this event. Irequest in writing: 1. A patient-safety / incident report 2. Service and downtime recordsfor this MRI unit for the two cancelled appointments and the date of this exam 3. Namesof the technologist and supervisor 4. Confirmation that progressive heating reported bya patient was logged 5. Confirmation whether the scanner was inspected after the priorbreakdowns and after this exam before it was used again 6. Options to complete theMRI on a different machine, with a different technologist, or at a different site, with acall bulb issued and tested before the scan (b)(6).

product_problems: Insufficient Device Problem Information
records.text: Philips received a report that a 69-year-old female patient sustained a second-degree thermal burn with blistering on the upper left arm during an MRI examination. During the scan, the patient experienced an intense sensation of heat and activated the nurse call button. Following completion of the examination, a burn injury measuring approximately 1 × 3 cm with blister formation was identified. The reported injury was documented with supporting photographs, a second degree burn with a blister >2.5 cm occurred. The patient was treated with a cool, damp cloth to the affected area. Given the severity of the injury, the presence of a second-degree burn with blistering, and the inability to rule out the potential for permanent impairment, the event meets the criteria for a serious injury. Therefore, this event has been determined to be reportable. Philips has started an investigation, a follow up report will be submitted once the investigation has been completed.

product_problems: Improper or Incorrect Procedure or Method
records.text: Siemens Healthineers (Siemens) was notified of a potential patient injury associated with a MAGNETOM Altea MRI system. According to the report, the patient complained of hearing issues following an MRI examination on (b)(6)2026. The patient wore only headphones during the scan and did not use the combination of headphones and earplugs specified for hearing protection. It was confirmed that the hearing protection warning signage was posted on the examination room door. The patient was evaluated by an ENT specialist on (b)(6)2026. Based on additional information received on September 2, 2026, Siemens was informed by the customer that the patient was diagnosed with Stage 2 temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorder. The customer indicated that no additional information is available from the patient's ENT specialist or directly from the patient. The customer also confirmed that the patient did not use the hearing protection prescribed in the system Instructions for Use and wore only the standard Siemens headphones during the examination. As sufficient information is not available to rule out the occurrence of a serious injury, this event is being reported. H3, H6: The investigation is ongoing. A supplemental report will be submitted upon receipt of additional reportable information and/or investigation completion.H6: Component Code G07002 was utilized for hearing protection.

product_problems: Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem
records.text: Philips received a report that a patient suffered tinnitus as a result of an MR examination back in Oct 2025. This complaint concerns the (allegation of) occurrence of an acoustic noise-related incident to a patient while using a Philips MR system. The patient indicated he suffers tinnitus since the MR scan that was performed in Oct 2025 on a Philips MR system. The patient had pre-existing mild tinnitus. According to the hospital, the patient was given earplugs and headphones and a lab technician checked whether the hearing protection was working properly using a sound test prior to the examination. The event was not reported to Philips in Oct 2025, the event was identified based on a news article about a court case.Most likely the product operated as intended. No logfile analysis was possible as the incident took place Oct 2025, logfiles from this date are no longer available on the device. No service activity was identified around the time of the event. The risks associated with acoustic noise (i.e. normal condition risks) are identified and assessed in the Risk Management File. The Instructions for Use (IfU) contains a number of warnings and cautions to assist operators in avoiding acoustic noise-related incidents. Labeling is compliant with all regulatory requirements.It is known that the acoustic noise level of an MR system may be high enough to cause discomfort when no adequate hearing protection is applied. Philips MR scanners fulfill the requirements as formulated in the IEC60601-2-33 standard with respect to the allowed maximum acoustic noise production and are designed to be quieter than the level set in this standard. Adequate hearing protection is necessary to reduce the risk of hearing impairment. The IfU contains safety information for the user.CONCLUSION: There was no indication of a MR system malfunction mentioned which could have contributed to the incident. Therefore, it was concluded that high levels of acoustic noise during normal operation could have caused the worsening of the pre-existing tinnitus.
